subject: Recap: throughput & p95 targets — next asks
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Ava Thompson <ava.thompson@xcorp.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@xcorp.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: throughput & p95 targets — next asks

Hi Ava / Samir,

Thanks again for the call today — good to meet the infra and product teams. Short recap below (TL;DR at top) and a concise list of what we need to size a POC.

TL;DR: Primary pain is inconsistent p95 during streaming inference (chat UI) when concurrency spikes beyond ~60 simultaneous users; target p95 <= 300ms for assistant completions, current p95 ~900ms depending on session length. Constraints: preserve streaming partial responses, use your current model family (open-llm v2-13B quantized), single-region (us-west-2) deployment.

What we covered:
- Current stack: browser websocket -> Node multiplexing -> single Triton endpoint per model. No prefix/KV caching across sessions; cache cleared on reconnects.
- Symptoms: p95 spikes during peak window (11:00–13:00 PDT); queue depth increases, memory pressure, and GPU context switching observed.
- Desired success metrics (your stated goals):
  * p95 <= 300ms for completions up to 512 tokens
  * sustained throughput >= 6k tokens/s (99th percentile across pool)
  * streaming UX: partial tokens sent as they’re produced (no batch-waiting >50ms)
  * fallback behavior: graceful degrade to smaller model variant under overload without breaking the streaming contract

Immediate asks from XCorp (to move sizing forward):
1) Sample anonymized per-minute concurrency and mean session length for a representative week (CSV).
2) Confirm the model binary details: v2-13B-qt8 (exact quantization), and whether you can test a 4-bit variant for cost/latency experiments.
3) Any hard SLOs around token-level interactivity (e.g., max intertoken gap) vs overall completion p95 — this affects batching/continuous-run strategy.
4) Confirmation of security constraints for a POC (VPC peering allowed? IP allowlist?)

Next steps from Redwood:
- We’ll produce a sizing note and a 2-week POC plan (baseline + config experiments: batching, prefix caching, KV-resident tuning).
- Draft MOP and cost estimate by Wed (2026-10-14).
- Proposed POC kickoff window: Oct 19–Nov 2.

Attachments referenced: xcorp_latency_profile.csv (placeholder), initial-mop-outline.pdf (stub).

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Natarajan

Subject: Re: Recap: throughput & p95 targets — next asks

Thanks Priya — this is helpful and aligns with what our product team is seeing. A few clarifications below.

- We can provide the per-minute concurrency CSV for last two weeks; will scrub user ids and send by EOD tomorrow.
- Model: we currently run v2-13B-qt8 in production. We can stand up a 4-bit test variant in a sandbox cluster, but procurement needs a short PR to approve access (should be fine for POC).
- Streaming SLOs: product insists on token-level interactivity — they want max intertoken gap < 120ms for perceived fluidity, otherwise users complain. The 300ms completion p95 is more of a business metric.
- VPC peering: allowed for sandbox POC.

Couple of asks from our side: can Redwood run an initial sim with the CSV and propose an expected p95 curve for both current config and with prefix caching? Also, pricing ballpark for a 2-week POC (GPU-hours + engineering time) would help us prep the internal exec ask.

Best,
Ava
